mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 3% does not correlate with subsequent Fed tightening actions.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a decline in consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS MoM decline does not correlate with subsequent SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO MoM increase does not correlate with subsequent SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month, combined with an increase in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% quarter-over-quarter and the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals a potential economic slowdown with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: economic slowdown with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
